purpose: Filgrastim-aafi helps your body make more white blood cells, which are the cells that fight infections. It is often used when certain cancer treatments, like chemotherapy, lower your white blood cell count too much. It can also be used in other conditions where your body does not make enough of these important infection-fighting cells.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a protein called G-CSF that tells your bone marrow to produce more white blood cells. This medication works just like that natural protein, signaling your bone marrow to ramp up production of white blood cells called neutrophils. Having more neutrophils helps protect you from serious infections.
common_side_effects: Bone or muscle aches and pain (especially in the back, hips, or legs) are the most common side effects. You may also experience headache, tiredness, nausea, or redness and soreness at the injection site. These effects are usually manageable and often improve as your body adjusts.
warnings: In rare cases, this medication can cause a serious condition called spleen rupture, so tell your doctor right away if you have sudden, severe pain in the upper left belly or left shoulder. It can also cause a rare but serious lung problem called ARDS — get help immediately if you have trouble breathing. Let your doctor know if you have sickle cell disease, as this medication may trigger a painful crisis. Do not shake the medication, as this can damage it.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous) or into a vein (intravenous), usually once daily. The dose is based on your weight and the condition being treated. Your doctor or nurse will determine the right dose and show you how to give the injection at home if needed. Treatment usually starts the day after chemotherapy ends and continues for several days until your white blood cell count recovers.
